kccs.title: Electrophilicity & metabolic activation
kccs.description: Is electrophilic or can be metabolically activated to electrophiles that form covalent adducts with macromolecules.
kccs.mechanism: Compounds undergo phase-I metabolic activation (often via CYP450) to produce reactive intermediates that covalently bind nucleophilic sites in DNA, RNA, and proteins.

kccs.title: Genotoxicity
kccs.description: Induces DNA damage including strand breaks, mutations, micronuclei, chromosomal aberrations, or DNA-protein crosslinks.
kccs.mechanism: Direct or indirect induction of DNA lesions detectable in standardized genotoxicity batteries; high concordance with carcinogenicity in long-term rodent bioassays.

kccs.title: Altered DNA repair / genomic instability
kccs.description: Alters DNA repair capacity or causes large-scale genomic instability (e.g. aneuploidy, polyploidy, chromothripsis).
kccs.mechanism: Indirect carcinogens may not damage DNA themselves but compromise repair fidelity or chromosomal segregation, amplifying mutational burden over time.

kccs.title: Epigenetic alterations
kccs.description: Induces changes in DNA methylation, histone modification, or non-coding RNA expression that persist across cell divisions.
kccs.mechanism: Heritable changes in gene expression without alteration of DNA sequence; can silence tumor suppressors or activate oncogenes long after exposure.

kccs.title: Oxidative stress
kccs.description: Induces oxidative stress via ROS/RNS, mitochondrial dysfunction, or depletion of antioxidant defenses.
kccs.mechanism: Excess reactive species cause oxidative DNA lesions, lipid peroxidation, and signaling dysregulation; chronic ROS exposure is mechanistically linked to multiple tumor types.

kccs.title: Chronic inflammation
kccs.description: Induces or sustains chronic inflammation through cytokine release, immune cell recruitment, or persistent tissue injury.
kccs.mechanism: Sustained inflammatory microenvironments produce ROS/RNS, growth factors, and immunosuppressive signals that promote initiation, promotion, and progression.

kccs.title: Immunosuppression
kccs.description: Is immunosuppressive — decreases immune surveillance against transformed cells.
kccs.mechanism: Reduced immune surveillance permits clonal expansion of pre-neoplastic cells; particularly relevant for virally-driven and skin malignancies.

kccs.title: Receptor-mediated effects
kccs.description: Modulates nuclear receptors (AhR, ER, AR, PPAR, etc.) or membrane receptors in ways that drive proliferation or differentiation.
kccs.mechanism: Ligand-receptor interactions produce sustained transcriptional reprogramming; especially important for hormone-dependent tissues.

kccs.title: Immortalization
kccs.description: Causes immortalization via telomerase activation or bypass of replicative senescence.
kccs.mechanism: Activation of telomere-maintenance pathways or inactivation of p53/Rb axis enables indefinite proliferative capacity — a hallmark of malignancy.

kccs.title: Altered proliferation, death & nutrient supply
kccs.description: Alters cell proliferation, cell death, angiogenesis, or nutrient supply in the tissue microenvironment.
kccs.mechanism: Imbalance between proliferation and apoptosis, coupled with neovascularization and metabolic rewiring, supports tumor outgrowth and expansion.

kccs.title: Microbiome alteration
kccs.description: Alters composition or function of the host microbiota in ways linked to carcinogenesis.
kccs.mechanism: Recently proposed KCC. Dysbiosis can promote local inflammation, generate genotoxic metabolites (e.g. colibactin), and modulate xenobiotic metabolism.

kccs.title: Cellular senescence
kccs.description: Induces premature cellular senescence and a pro-tumorigenic senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP).
kccs.mechanism: Senescent cells secrete a pro-inflammatory, pro-mitogenic milieu (SASP) that can paradoxically promote proliferation and invasion of neighboring cells.

kccs.title: Altered stem-cell dynamics
kccs.description: Disrupts normal stem- or progenitor-cell behavior, including self-renewal, lineage commitment, or niche signaling.
kccs.mechanism: Expansion or mis-differentiation of tissue stem cells generates a larger pool of long-lived cells susceptible to mutation accumulation.

kccs.title: Disrupted intercellular communication
kccs.description: Disrupts gap-junction intercellular communication (GJIC) or other tissue-level signaling.
kccs.mechanism: Loss of GJIC removes a key homeostatic constraint, allowing initiated cells to escape growth control imposed by neighboring normal cells.

columnDefinitions.definition: The assay endpoint provides context to what biomarker/outcome measured by a particular assay is indicative of, and how it relates back to the broader KC/KC-subgrouping. For example, DNA adducts measured using [32P]-Postlabelling techniques indicate DNA damage ('Assay endpoint'). If within a given study the specific DNA adducts being measured are known to be caused by by-products of oxidative radicals, the KC subgroup provides context to the associated KC: 'oxidative damage to DNA'.

Additional sub-grouping of the KC endpoints, if applicable. For example, an assay may be used to measure a specific type of lipid peroxidation product (a by-product of reactive oxygen species reacting with cellular lipids and thus denoted as being the secondary assay endpoint, 'Assay endpoint II'). This by-product's relevance to a chemical's carcinogenic potential is its propensity to react with nucleophilic sites in DNA (DNA damage thus being primary assay endpoint for this assay, 'Assay endpoint I'.).

See row above, 'Assay endpoint III" offers additional subgrouping if deemed appropriate. For example, study authors may use methylation-specific PCR to confirm methylation status of CpG within the promoter region of a gene related with homologous recombination ('Assay endpoint III"). Methylation status may alter mRNA expression of this critical cell regulatory/DNA repair gene ('Assay Endpoint II'). The primary assay endpoint relating the given chemical agent's relation to KCs is thus "Locus-specific DNA methylation" (Assay endpoint I).
Indicates as to whether another stimulant or acitvation agent was applied to the experimental test system, required for carrying out the assay or demonstrating a particular effect
Indicates as to whether an assay is applied to a primary cell, primary tissue, a cell line, a cultured cell, or is cell-free
Cell type or specific cell line in which assay is conducted/biomarker is measured
Study author and year of reference publication
DOI of any references used, if applicable
Experimental design in which assay may be applied
Indicates if an immortalized cell line is used ('Yes')
Primary key characteristic of carcinogens
Major endpoints associated with the key characteristic
Additional sub-grouping of the KC subgroup, if applicable
Indication as to whether an assay is to be conducted in exclusively mammalian cells (or vice versa) per a particular reference (including test guidelines)
Name or description of assay/method applied

Any additional details of the assay may be indicated here. This may either be a particular instrument, a specific method developed by a research team, etc. Many methods require the use of an additional technology
IARC monograph in which assay is referenced, if applicable
Monograph chemical agent
Associated OECD Test Guideline number, if applicable
Additonal experimental design information, as to whether assay is applied in humans vs. animals vs. plants, etc., including those that may be conducted ex vivo and in vitro.
PMID of any references used, if applicable
Other associated key characteristic

Indication as to whether an assay referenced within a publication/test guideline is to be conducted in a particular species for 'Animal' studies (or biological order - such as rodents). If the organism is 'Human', species is denoted as 'NA'.

Substance (e.g. mitogen, cytokine, cell type, virus, hormone, etc.) used to provoke a specific biological response in cells or tissue. This is commonly used in immunological applications, such as  to assess a chemical agents effect on allergic response.
Cell line type used to evaluate the activity of various immune effector cells, such as cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs), natural killer (NK) cells, and natural cytotoxicity (NC) assays
Tissue type in which assay is conducted/biomarker is measured (if applicable)
Additional tissue type information
Indicates if a transgenic cell line is used ('Yes')
